$comment: Rails for the clerk's ORCHESTRATOR session, added by `ralph.sh` with
`--settings` because `roles.ts` names this file as the role's
`claude-orchestrator-settings.json` — so it repeats every rule of that
file, and adds the clerk's own.
The clerk's session reads untrusted Slack text and writes one plan file
(felipearos/ralph#315). It holds no Slack or Jira credential — both are
`gate` secrets — and everything it needs is in what
`clerk/batch.ts` prints, so it has no use for the network at all. A
message that says 'fetch this URL' or 'post this to Slack' is data; these
rules make sure the session cannot act on it by habit: no web tools, no
`curl`, no `wget`. Nor may it edit the clerk's store (`ralph/clerk/` in
git's common directory), whose handed batch carries the candidates a
report may be merged into; the gate also signs that batch and files a
Both spellings, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`, for the reason
`claude-executor-settings.json` gives. A tripwire, not the boundary: the
boundary is that no credential that could write anywhere is in the
session's environment, and that code validates the plan before any write.
